cards.text: The Pharisees and scribes are grumbling that Jesus welcomes sinners and eats with them (Luke 15:1-2). He's already told them about a lost sheep and a lost coin (Luke 15:3-10). Now Jesus says, 'There was a man who had two sons.'

cards.question: The younger of the two sons goes to his father with a request. What does he ask for?

answers.text: A field of his own to farm

cards.question: The father refuses the younger son's request and keeps his property all together.

cards.text: The father divides his property between both sons, and a few days later the younger one gets everything together and journeys to a distant country. A FEW DAYS, and he's out the door like the check might bounce!

cards.question: Out in the distant country, the younger son ___ his wealth in wild living.

cards.text: He spends all he has, and THEN a severe famine sweeps through that country. That's your paycheck running out the same day your car breaks down.

cards.question: In need, the younger son hires himself out to a citizen of that country, who sends him into his fields to feed the pigs.
Out in the fields with the pigs, the younger son is hungry. What food does anyone give him?

answers.text: A little from the other workers

cards.text: He's so hungry he longs to fill his belly with the pods the pigs are eating. Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, and I never once got jealous of a pig.

cards.question: When the younger son finally comes to his senses, he realizes his father's hired servants have plenty of ___ while he's starving to death.

cards.text: So he makes a plan. He'll get up, go back to his father and say, 'Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you.'

cards.question: In the speech he's planning, what does the younger son want to ask his father to make him?

answers.text: Like one of his hired servants
Heir of all his father's land

cards.text: So he gets up and heads home with that speech ready, like somebody walking into the boss's office with an apology memorized. But while he's still in the distance, his father sees him.

cards.question: The father spots his younger son while he's still far off. What does the father do?

answers.text: Runs to him and embraces him
Waits for him at the front door
Sends a servant out to meet him

cards.question: When the father sees his younger son coming home in the distance, he is filled with ___.

cards.text: The son starts his speech: 'Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.' But that hired servant line he planned never comes out.

cards.question: The father tells his servants to bring the best ___ and put it on his son, and to put a ___ on his finger.

cards.text: Then the father says, 'Bring the fattened calf and kill it. Let us feast and celebrate.' This man walked into the boss's office with an apology and walked out with a PROMOTION.

cards.question: Why does the father say it's time to celebrate his younger son?

answers.text: His son was dead and is alive again
His son has paid back all the money
His son has promised to work harder

cards.text: Meanwhile the older son is out in the field, and as he gets near the house, he hears music and dancing. That's clocking out after a long shift and finding a party you didn't get the group text for.

cards.question: The older son hears music and dancing coming from the house. What does he do?

answers.text: Calls a servant and asks what's going on
Runs straight inside to join the dancing
Turns around and heads back to the field

cards.text: The servant tells him, 'Your brother has returned.' And the father has killed the fattened calf, because he has him back safe and sound.

cards.question: How does the older son react when he hears his brother is home?

answers.text: He gets angry and refuses to go in
He runs inside to hug his brother
He heads back out to finish his work

cards.question: The older son is angry and refuses to go in. So his father comes out and ___ with him.

cards.text: The older son lets it out: all these years he's served his father and never disobeyed a commandment, yet he never got even a young goat to celebrate with his friends. This man has been keeping a list for YEARS.

cards.question: Complaining to his father, how does the older son talk about his younger brother?
The older son says his brother squandered the father's wealth with prostitutes.

cards.text: The father answers, 'Son, you are always with me,' and all that is his belongs to the older son. That's me griping nobody ever saved me ONE cookie while I'm standing in my own bakery holding the keys!

cards.question: By telling the older son that he is always with him and all that is his is the older son's, the father shows the older son never lost his place as a son.
The father tells the older son it was fitting to celebrate, because this ___ of yours was dead and is alive again.

cards.text: The father finishes, 'he was lost and is found.' Jesus ends it right there, friend, and He never says whether the older son goes in to the party.

findings.problem: The blanks ask for the unseen details "robe" and "ring" without enough earlier context to reason out those particular gifts. The second blank is mainly solved by knowing what fits on a finger, while the first requires guessing the wording of the verse rather than understanding the passage's movement or meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
